title: Review: Elimination; Carbon–carbon bond formation and organic synthesis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR11#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR26a#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR11#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR26a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR11#N.11, OR26a#N.11, OR11#N.9, OR26a#N.4, OR11#N.2, OR26a#N.13, OR11#N.5, OR26a#N.8a. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Nucleophile
items.clue: Role of OH⁻ when it donates a lone pair to a δ+ carbon atom.

items.label: Propanenitrile
items.clue: CH₃CH₂CN, made by refluxing bromoethane with KCN in ethanol.

items.label: Base
items.clue: Role of OH⁻ when it accepts H⁺ from the carbon next to the C–Br carbon.

items.label: Hydroxynitrile
items.clue: Formed when CN⁻ adds across the C=O of an aldehyde or ketone, e.g. CH₃CH(OH)CN.

questions.stem: Chlorocyclohexane is warmed with aqueous sodium hydroxide in one tube, and heated under reflux with sodium hydroxide in ethanol in another. The main product in the second tube is cyclohexene. Which statement explains the second result?

options.text: In ethanol, OH⁻ bonds to the δ+ carbon of the C–Cl bond, and Cl⁻ leaves.
In ethanol, the solvent removes HCl from chlorocyclohexane, and OH⁻ just neutralises the HCl.
In ethanol, OH⁻ mainly acts as a base, removing H⁺ from a carbon next to the C–Cl carbon.
In ethanol, the ring opens as OH⁻ breaks a C–C bond, and a gaseous product is released.

questions.stem: Which pair of reactants, in dry ether followed by dilute acid, gives butan-2-ol, CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃?

options.text: CH₃MgBr and propanone
CH₃CH₂MgBr and methanal
CH₃CH₂MgBr and carbon dioxide
CH₃CH₂MgBr and ethanal

questions.explanation: The ethyl group bonds to the C=O carbon of ethanal: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃, a secondary alcohol.

questions.stem: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, (CH₃)₂CBrCH₂CH₃, is heated with ethanolic potassium hydroxide. How many different alkenes can form?
questions.explanation: H from a CH₃ gives 2-methylbut-1-ene. H from the CH₂ gives 2-methylbut-2-ene. Its C2 carries two CH₃ groups, so it has no E/Z isomers.

questions.stem: 1-Bromobutane is heated under reflux with potassium cyanide in ethanol. What is the organic product?

options.text: Butanenitrile
Pentan-1-amine
Pentanenitrile
Butan-1-ol

questions.explanation: CN⁻ replaces Br: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CN. Five carbons, including the C≡N carbon.

questions.stem: 2-bromopropane is heated under reflux with potassium hydroxide dissolved in ethanol, and propene forms. What is the role of the hydroxide ion?

options.text: It is a nucleophile: it donates a lone pair to the carbon bonded to Br.
It is an electrophile: it accepts a pair of electrons from the C–Br bond.
It is a base: it accepts H⁺ from a carbon next to the C–Br carbon.
It is a catalyst: it is given back at the end, so it is written over the arrow.

questions.explanation: OH⁻ takes an H⁺ from the neighbouring carbon and becomes H₂O. Br⁻ leaves, and a C=C forms between the two carbons.

questions.stem: Bromomethane, CH₃Br, has one carbon. Which route turns it into ethylamine, CH₃CH₂NH₂?

options.text: Heat with excess ammonia in ethanol in a sealed tube
Reflux with KCN in ethanol, then hydrolyse with dilute acid
Reflux with KCN in ethanol, then reduce the nitrile
Warm with aqueous NaOH, then heat the product with ammonia

questions.explanation: CN⁻ adds one carbon: CH₃CN, ethanenitrile. Reduction turns –C≡N into –CH₂NH₂: CH₃CH₂NH₂.

questions.stem: A chemist wants as much propene, and as little propan-2-ol, as possible from 2-bromopropane. Which conditions should be used?

options.text: Aqueous potassium hydroxide, warmed gently
Aqueous silver nitrate in ethanol, warmed
Potassium hydroxide with ultraviolet light, at room temperature
Potassium hydroxide dissolved in ethanol, heated under reflux

questions.explanation: Ethanol as the solvent and a high temperature favour OH⁻ acting as a base. Some propan-2-ol still forms, as the two reactions compete.

questions.stem: 2-Hydroxypropanenitrile, CH₃CH(OH)CN, is heated under reflux with dilute hydrochloric acid. What is the organic product?

options.text: Propanoic acid
1-Aminopropan-2-ol
Ammonium 2-hydroxypropanoate
2-Hydroxypropanoic acid

questions.explanation: C≡N → –COOH, with NH₄Cl as the by-product. CH₃CH(OH)COOH is lactic acid.
